top.title: 30 Years Later, Star Trek's Greatest 'Next Generation' Movie Is Officially Free to Stream
top.description: Turning a successful television series into a movie isn't as easy as just giving the cast a bigger budget and adding in more explosions. What works on the small screen doesn't always translate to theaters, especially when filmmakers lose sight of what made audiences fall in love with the characters in the first place. Fortunately, Star Trek : First Contact understood that bigger could be better, provided the spectacle didn't come at the expense of the characters.

top.title: Maresca praises Arsenal but hopes Man City can match champions
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca gestures during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester City and Napoli at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Maresca praises Arsenal but hopes Man City can match champions») Mike Egerton/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca accepts Manchester City are some way behind Arsenal in their development - but is determined to match the champions this weekend. City, who travel to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday, have fallen six points behind the Gunners at the top of the Premier League after failing to win their last four matches. It is an abrupt downturn in form after City opened their campaign with seven successive victories, but Maresca believes their relative lack of experience together helps explain their recent difficulties. The City manager, who succeeded Pep Guardiola in the summer, said: “They won the Premier League, played the Champions League final, so that shows how good they are in this moment. “We’re going to try our best to win the game but no doubt in this moment, because they won the Premier League, they are the best. “For two-and-a-half months we were top of the league. Now we are not there and everyone is comparing. That is correct but, for me, it is seven years together against four months together. You cannot compare. “We already showed [our strength] this season in winning important games away – at Old Trafford and Anfield, two important away games. “Sunday is another important one, we showed already and we can win again.” Maresca says he has been happy enough with his side’s general play, but their failure to convert chances and occasional defensive lapses are proving costly. He said: “The problem for us has been [the difference] between what we create and what we concede. “We need to try to be solid, don’t concede, and with the quality that we have, and the amount of chances that we create every game, for sure we need to be more clinical and score more goals. “We need to win duels, second balls and show personality, but this is a nice game for us to see where we are in term of personality and to try to understand the situation more.” City can ill afford to lose if they are to keep pace with the Gunners but Maresca is more concerned about the bigger picture than the immediate ramifications for the title race. He said: “Because we won seven or eight games in a row at the beginning the transition looks more easy, but it is a transition. “Where we can be on Sunday night if we win or draw is important, 100%, but for us it’s a long season and we will see where are in February or March and from there you can set the goals. “Now it’s useless to speak about a target or where we can be at the end of the season.”

top.title: In defence of Red Bull and its footballing exploits
top.description: In defence of Red Bull and its footballing exploits As the Bundesliga’s most controversial member, Die Roten Bullen continue to operate effectively in a hostile environment. Measuring success strictly through silverware is a difficult task, but combing through historic transfer business – in some cases via picturesque Salzburg – tells a rather specific tale. Defined by exits more so than arrivals, the club appears to provide a platform for talent while consistently living up to the brand’s familiar slogan. Dayot Upamecano, arguably the most adept central defender at this moment in time, departed for Bavaria after four seasons in Leipzig. Joshua Kimmich plied his trade there, firstly in 3. Liga and 2. Bundesliga before eventually coming of age in Bayern colours. One other Munich-based player, the plucky and tenacious Konrad Laimer, spent six campaigns in that divisive shirt prior to his free transfer. It has to be said that this is the tip of one very profitable iceberg. Just this summer, the notable sale of Yan Diomande to José Mourinho’s star-studded Real Madrid brought in approximately €125 million alone. Combining last year’s fees for Benjamin Šeško and Xavi Simons, both to the Premier League, equals a similar amount. Factoring in the previous departures of Joško Gvardiol, Dominik Szoboszlai and Christopher Nkunku during a single window also amounts to an eye-watering figure. Credit is due on the recruitment side, of course. However, one important question remains: is it all down to coincidence, or an intense top-down philosophy that allows and actively encourages individuals to showcase their true potential? Extending from Austria to places such as Bragantino and New York, the network Red Bull controls is truly global – one might say a world away from the state of Saxony. In relation to fan ownership and a deeply ingrained ‘50+1’ culture, it may come across as cold or overly commercial. Compare it to some of the financial nightmares at clubs in England and their model suddenly seems rational, progressive and sustainable. Naturally, a willingness to bypass the system that many regard to be the spirit of German football left a lasting impression. Supporters with a deep, long-standing connection to what was once SSV Markranstädt will no doubt feel pangs of betrayal. Also, the same could easily be said for Die Mozartstädter or lovers of ‘soccer’ in the Big Apple. While yet to claim a domestic crown, Leipzig have made serious progress in other areas. Lifting the DFB-Pokal consecutively is no mean feat, especially when you consider the fact that Bayern Munich only returned to Berlin last season for the first time in just over half a decade. Competing in Europe on a regular basis brings elites to Red Bull Arena and sees the side visit historic stadiums, even under that adjusted crest. top.title: George Russell says Lewis Hamilton offers a different example from Max Verstappen
top.description: Motorsport photo In an exclusive Sky Sports F1 interview with Martin Brundle - previewed Friday ahead of its full broadcast before Sunday’s Qatar Grand Prix - George Russell addressed his reignited Las Vegas feud with the four-time world champion Max Verstappen by drawing a quiet, unmistakable contrast between two of Formula 1’s modern giants. "He [Verstappen] is a ruthless competitor, and I massively respect that, but there's also Lewis Hamilton, who I've spent three years team-mates with and watched my whole life," Russell said. "And obviously Toto [Wolff, Mercedes' team principal] spent 12 years with [Hamilton], who is equally a ruthless competitor and absolute animal behind the wheel, but obviously has incredible values and grace and dignity. "And Lewis is somebody who I really look up to and who is an incredible role model for young kids coming through. But there is no right or wrong; there's just opinions. Everyone has different opinions, and some people like driver A and some people like driver B, and as I've grown older, I don't really let it affect me as much." Why the Hamilton benchmark carries real weight The comparison hits harder because Russell lived it firsthand. Across 68 shared starts as Mercedes team-mates from 2022 through 2024, Russell and Hamilton fought on razor-thin margins: deadlocked 34–34 in race finishes, separated by just two total points (697 to 695 in Hamilton’s favour), with Russell holding a 39–29 edge in qualifying. Even when tensions briefly flared on track - such as their opening-lap tangle at Losail in 2023 - the pairing never descended into public character attacks. Verstappen’s Las Vegas response last weekend could hardly have been more different. After Russell called out Verstappen’s driving following their Turn 14 final-practice brush - an incident that earned the Red Bull driver a formal FIA warning for erratic driving - Verstappen won Saturday night’s race while Russell locked up late and clipped the Turn 5 barrier battling team-mate Kimi Antonelli, falling to ninth. Speaking to Dutch broadcaster Viaplay, he went even further: "His comments don't motivate me, because he's nowhere near me. All talk off the track and a complete joke on it this season. Perfect karma." Reflecting on the fallout with Brundle, Russell accepted that winning gives Verstappen the microphone - while emphasising where their personalities diverge. top.title: Xabi Alonso admits Chelsea are low on confidence after third straight defeat at Nottingham Forest
top.description: Xabi Alonso admits Chelsea are low on confidence after third straight defeat at Nottingham Forest Xabi Alonso has admitted that Chelsea are low on confidence after losing 3-2 at Nottingham Forest. Chelsea lost a third consecutive game at the City Ground on Friday night as the club's poor run of form continued. Igor Jesus volleyed Forest ahead inside five minutes, before Morgan Gibbs-White doubled the lead from the penalty spot early in the second half, after Wesley Fofana brought down former Chelsea forward Liam Delap in the area. Emmanuel Emegha pulled one back for the Blues, but a second from Gibbs-White restored Forest's advantage. Emegha was on target again, heading home from Cole Palmer's cross, but Chelsea were unable to find an equaliser. Defeat increases the pressure on Alonso, whose side have now conceded 23 goals in just 12 league games. Only Crystal Palace have conceded more in the Premier League , ahead of the weekend's fixtures. Chelsea are eighth in the Premier League table, five points adrift of the Champions League places, having played a game more than fourth-placed Liverpool. Alonso urges Chelsea to find solutions after Forest defeat extends losing streak to three games Reflecting on the result, Alonso said his side are suffering from a crisis of confidence. "Many things didn’t go the way we wanted," the Spaniard said in his post-match interview. "I think we are low in confidence; you see that the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting [a goal back for] the 2-1, we then conceded the 3-1 just when we had a little bit of boost from the goal. "We can do better for sure. At this level, you need to hold results and you don’t have to concede that much. That is why we are losing the last games. "So, everything is not going our way. We are responsible for that, and we are responsible for trying to find solutions."

top.title: Gaza’s chess players survive a genocide and rebuild a community
top.description: Gaza City – Raghad Rabie, 18, never expected to beat her chess coach, Raghad Adas, at chess. During the friendly match, Rabie deliberately left some of her pieces exposed to distract her opponent as she planned a move that would deliver a checkmate in two turns. Her strategy worked, giving her confidence in her abilities as a chess player. But the match also reflected something bigger: The return of chess to Gaza after the Israeli genocide devastated sporting activities across the enclave. Rabie began learning chess in August 2025, when she was displaced in southern Gaza. Looking for something new to learn and a way to occupy her time, she taught herself the basic rules online before joining a training course run by Adas. “I had admired chess players for a long time and wanted to learn the game. I started on my own, then the course helped me improve,” she says. She has since participated in two tournaments and dreams of becoming a chess grandmaster, the goal of every serious chess player, and representing Palestine internationally. But pursuing that ambition in Gaza, still under an Israeli siege and subject to daily air attacks despite an October 2025 “ceasefire”, is difficult. There is no permanent training venue for chess players, so weekly gatherings take place in different locations, including the Lord Cafe in the al-Rimal neighbourhood of Gaza City. Raghad Rabie, 18, one of the chess players at Stalemate [Lina Abu Zayed/Al Jazeera] To become an International Chess Federation (FIDE)-rated grandmaster, as Rabie hopes, requires thousands of hours of dedicated practice and study. But a shortage of chessboards, clocks and chess books – and soaring prices for any available chess equipment – has made this mission difficult. Before the war, Adas was captain of the girls’ Spark team, playing in Palestinian Chess Federation tournaments. She was also among 10 players selected to take part in matches against other Palestinians from the occupied West Bank with the goal of forming a national team, which it was hoped would compete internationally. Travel arrangements and permit procedures had been completed, but then Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza broke out in October 2023, killing at least 74,000 Palestinians and laying waste to the Palestinian enclave. “I was excited about taking part in an international tournament, but the war made everything much more difficult,” Adas told Al Jazeera. Adas said the team’s headquarters was destroyed, its players were scattered across Gaza, and she lost contact with several former teammates amid the forced Israeli displacements. About a year after the war began, Adas started teaching chess in shelters, initially volunteering before working with organisations and eventually continuing her mission independently. She noticed a growing interest in the sport among newcomers, as well as the return of players who had stopped playing during the genocide. top.title: Lakers are ‘real’ deal — even Victor Wembanyama thinks so
top.description: Like the rest of us, Victor Wembanyama was skeptical of the Lakers. The darlings of the NBA entered Friday’s game against the Spurs with the top record in the NBA at 15-3. But they hadn’t played the league’s most elite teams. They hadn’t really proven themselves. So, Friday was a temperature check. It was a harsh dressing room mirror that would expose their flaws in front of a national television audience. How did they do? “As a team I wasn’t sure what they were built of, at least from the start of the season,” Wembanyama acknowledged. “But it’s real.” The Lakers lost, 99-96 . But the final score was far less important than what transpired. The Lakers led by as much as 20 points. They bottled up Wembanyama in the first half, holding him to just eight points on nine shot attempts and five rebounds. Over that period, Luka Dončić had as many rebounds as Wembanyama (five) while scoring more than twice as many points (19). It was incredible. The Spurs reached the Finals last year. Wembanyama is unequivocally considered the next face of the league once the 41-year-old LeBron James retires. This was about as big of a test as the Lakers could get. And at the beginning of the game, they were jaw-droppingly good. Then things fell apart. The Lakers were outscored in the third quarter, 30-14. Over that period, they were outshot from the field, 48.1% to 25%, and from beyond the 3-point line, 37.5% to 15.4%. They unraveled, culminating in Keldon Johnson making a 3-pointer with 1.8 seconds left to knot the score at 68-68 heading into the fourth quarter. The next 12 minutes were a dogfight. Both teams wanted this. Victor Wembanyama (left) and Luka Dončić look on during the Lakers’ 99-96 NBA Cup loss to the Spurs on Nov. 27, 2026, in San Antonio. NBAE via Getty Images Wembanyama and Dončić, who are in a two-horse race for the MVP Award , knew the stakes. Everyone on the court was acutely aware of the chatter this game would generate. They knew this contest meant so much more than another regular-season game in November. Ultimately, the Spurs clawed a few inches ahead as the final buzzer sounded. After Wembanyama’s sluggish start, he finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, four steals and two blocked shots. But he had as many field-goal attempts (25) as points. Dončić had a game-high 31 points, six rebounds, eight assists and three steals. But he went 1-for-13 from beyond the arc. Luka Dončić looks to make a move on De’Aaron Fox during the Lakers’ NBA Cup road loss to the Spurs. AP Photo/Darren Abate Both of them shined. Both of them struggled. The Spurs likely prevailed because they’ve experienced moments like this before. They were three wins away from a championship last year. If they hadn’t blown double-digit leads in all five of their games against the Knicks in the Finals, they would’ve been the reigning champions. top.title: Roma continue talks with Endrick’s entourage
top.description: Roma continue talks with Endrick’s entourage Roma has no intention of abandoning the pursuit of Endrick, despite José Mourinho’s position continuing to complicate a possible January move. Fabrizio Romano took to his YouTube channel to discuss the Brazilian striker’s future, confirming the Giallorossi’s contact with his team: “Roma have been calling for weeks, and I’m sure they will continue to do so.” The journalist explained that AC Milan also remains strongly interested in the 2006-born player, so much so that they initiated initial contact in August to try to position themselves for the upcoming transfer window. The Rossoneri continue to monitor the player, even in the summer, should the conditions for a January move not be met. Roma remains among the clubs interested, waiting to see if Real Madrid will change their position. The main obstacle remains Mourinho, who has publicly reiterated his desire to retain Endrick. This stance could prevent the Brazilian’s departure during the winter transfer window, although the coach himself has acknowledged that the final decision will rest with Real Madrid’s management. As Fabrizio Romano himself reported, Liverpool and Aston Villa also attempted to acquire the Brazilian over the summer, but both received negative responses from Real Madrid.

top.title: Red Sox Floated as Landing Spot for Former Yankees Two-Time All-Star
top.description: Red Sox Floated as Landing Spot for Former Yankees Two-Time All-Star originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Red Sox continue to see multiple free agents leave the board, including ones who can help them on both sides of the baseball. However, the Red Sox have also made some impressive moves this offseason, so they should feel pretty confident about what they've done so far. As the Red Sox look for ways to improve, doing so on the mound will be at the top of the priority list. After losing Sonny Gray to the Minnesota Twins, the Red Sox have an opportunity to land another right-hander who could come in and help. One interesting target is Clay Holmes, who has played for the New York Mets and New York Yankees, among other teams. “Yet another pitcher who was traded during the ‘26 season, Holmes made nine starts for both the Mets (2.39 ERA) and Cubs (4.25 ERA). After suffering a fractured right fibula on May 15 when he was struck by a comebacker against the Yankees, Holmes proved to be healthy when he returned. “His experiences in New York (Yankees and Mets) could set Holmes up well for a stint with the Red Sox. In ‘25, his first season with a significant amount of starts, Holmes proved he was up to the task (12-8, 3.53 ERA) for the Mets,” Ian Browne of MLB.com wrote . Holmes has been a very interesting player throughout his career, as he's proven he can be among the top starters in baseball. However, he's worked out of the bullpen for much of his career. He’s been a full-time starter only since 2025. Since then, he's had some up-and-down moments, but he was really good for the Mets in 2025, posting a 3.53 ERA in 166.2 innings. His strikeout stuff has certainly declined since his time as a reliever, though he never had great strikeout numbers. However, at 33 and likely not too expensive, he could be a decent option to pursue. top.title: Arsenal threaten Barcelona pursuit of 22-year-old Sporting defender – report
top.description: Arsenal threaten Barcelona pursuit of 22-year-old Sporting defender – report Arsenal have emerged as a potential rival to Barcelona in the pursuit of Sporting CP right-back Ivan Fresneda, with Mikel Arteta’s side making contact with the defender’s representatives as they plan for the future of their right flank. According to a report from The Athletic (h/t SPORT ), Arsenal view the 22-year-old Spaniard as a possible long-term successor to Ben White, and it is a development that could complicate Barcelona’s long-standing interest in a player they have followed since his breakthrough at Real Valladolid. Arsenal identify Fresneda as a future option at right back As reported by the outlet, Arsenal are assessing their right-back options as part of their longer-term squad planning. In this regard, Fresneda has attracted attention after establishing himself at Sporting and with the Spanish national team, where his development has gathered momentum following a difficult initial period in Portugal. Arsenal are also interested in signing Ivan Fresneda. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) The talented full-back has recorded four assists in 16 appearances this season, and his attacking contribution, age and potential to improve further have strengthened his appeal to clubs looking for a long-term defensive option. Arsenal’s interest is not limited to mere scouting, with reports indicating that the Premier League champions have already contacted his representatives, although no agreement or formal transfer bid has been confirmed. Barcelona have followed Fresneda since 2023 Fresneda is a familiar name to Barcelona’s sporting department. The Catalan club seriously considered signing him in the summer of 2023 , when he was still playing for Valladolid and regarded as one of Spain’s promising young full-backs. Barcelona ultimately chose to bring Joao Cancelo back to the club instead, while Fresneda moved to Sporting for a reported fee of around €9 million. His contract in Lisbon runs until June 2028. Barcelona are still keeping an eye on Ivan Fresneda. (Photo by Gualter Fatia/Getty Images) Interest from Barcelona has resurfaced in recent weeks , as reports from Portugal have indicated the Blaugrana are monitoring his progress, with sporting director Deco involved in assessing the defender. Simply put, Barcelona are looking for a long-term solution at right-back after considering other targets, including Pedro Porro. Sporting hold a strong position in the transfer battle Crucially, Fresneda’s improvement has also strengthened Sporting’s position, with the Portuguese club now keen to extend his contract until 2031 and retain an €80 million release clause, making a potential transfer difficult to negotiate. For Barcelona, Arsenal’s contact already poses a big problem, and if the player ultimately signs an extension with the Portuguese club, their pursuit could well and truly rest once and for all.

top.description: Longest scoring streaks in Premier League history Evanilson is enjoying the best goalscoring form of his Bournemouth career, with the Cherries' centre-forward having scored in six consecutive Premier League appearances. The 27-year-old will target a seventh successive game with a goal against Fulham this weekend, an achievement recorded on just 19 occasions in Premier League history. A longer run would put him among an exclusive group of players to have scored in eight or more consecutive appearances. Alexander Isak - Newcastle (8) Alexander Isak scored in eight consecutive games for Newcastle United between December 2024 and January 2025. The Swedish striker began his run with a goal in a 3-3 draw with Liverpool before scoring in wins over Leicester City and Brentford. He subsequently helped the Magpies to six consecutive victories, scoring 11 goals across the eight-game period, including a hat-trick against Ipswich Town. Jamie Vardy - Leicester City (8) No stranger to scoring streaks, Jamie Vardy went eight-in-a-row with a goal during the 2019/20 campaign. Leicester won all eight games across that spell, including a record-equalling 9-0 win away at Southampton that saw Vardy and teammate Ayoze Perez score hat-tricks. The Foxes' forward ended the campaign with 23 league goals to win the Premier League Golden Boot. Daniel Sturridge - Liverpool (8) Daniel Sturridge might be one of the Premier League's modern 'what if?' players. Injuries derailed what was a stunning start to his Liverpool career, as Sturridge scored 31 league goals in 43 games across his first 18 months at Anfield. Sturridge enjoyed a remarkable 2013/14 campaign, scoring in eight consecutive Premier League appearances as Liverpool challenged for the title. The forward struck 21 league goals that season, finishing behind teammate Luis Suarez in the Golden Boot standings. Ruud van Nistelrooy - Manchester United (8) Ruud van Nistelrooy features twice on this list of the longest scoring streaks in Premier League history. His first entry came during his debut season at Manchester United , when the Dutchman scored in eight consecutive league appearances between December 2001 and January 2002. Van Nistelrooy enjoyed a prolific first campaign at Old Trafford, scoring 36 goals in all competitions and earning the PFA Players' Player of the Year award. The Dutchman's scoring streak crossed two campaigns, as he ended the 2002/03 season on fire. top.title: Real Madrid superstar leaves a lasting impression on Paul Pogba: ‘What he does is really impressive’
top.description: Real Madrid superstar leaves a lasting impression on Paul Pogba: ‘What he does is really impressive’ Real Madrid have been in excellent form for the past couple of months, with Jose Mourinho’s side securing 10 consecutive victories. One player who has become increasingly influential during this run is Jude Bellingham, with the Englishman returning to his very best. Bellingham had a couple of seasons to forget with Los Blancos as he struggled with shoulder problems and couldn’t replicate the highs of his debut season in Spain. However, the 23-year-old now looks close to his best , scoring goals and providing assists that have proved decisive for his team. The midfielder’s resurgence has received considerable attention, and former Juventus star Paul Pogba has now spoken very highly of him. Pogba makes massive Bellingham admission In an interview, the French World Cup winner was asked to identify a midfielder from the current generation who particularly impressed him. “Midfielder to watch from this generation? Jude Bellingham,” the Frenchman said (h/t Madrid Xtra ). Jude Bellingham is hitting new heights at Real Madrid this season. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) Asked whether he saw similarities between their playing styles, Pogba went a step further, admitting that Bellingham has greater ability than he ever did. “I believe that he has way more ability, and he’s from a different generation. What he does on the pitch is really impressive.” Pogba made a name for himself as one of the most technically gifted and physically dominant midfielders in Europe. His exceptional passing range and creativity, along with his long-range shooting, made him one of the most important players for France under Didier Deschamps. Bellingham thriving under Mourinho His comments about Bellingham come at an excellent time, following the Englishman’s second-half heroics against PSV Eindhoven. Bellingham has been in excellent form since the 2026 World Cup. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Having begun the game on the bench, he came on in the second half and scored a spectacular goal to inspire Madrid’s 5-1 Champions League comeback. Beyond his goalscoring ability, Bellingham’s greatest strength lies in his versatility. He can carry the ball through midfield and contribute defensively, making him a complete midfielder. With players like Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva providing creativity around him, Mourinho has the perfect system to get the best out of Jude Bellingham. Just one goal short of matching his tally from the entire previous campaign, Bellingham will be eager to maintain his form in the coming months.

top.title: From England: Roma tracking Federico Chiesa
top.description: From England: Roma tracking Federico Chiesa New confirmation is coming from England regarding the future of Federico Chiesa, one of the wingers linked to Roma ahead of the January transfer window. According to The Athletic , the 1997-born player will leave Liverpool in 2027, either during the winter transfer window or at the end of the season. The former Juventus player is now on the fringes of Andoni Iraola’s coaching project, having only played two minutes of the Premier League match against Manchester City on October 11th since the start of the season. As reported in recent days by Corriere dello Sport, Chiesa has been offered to Roma, with Tony D’Amico working to provide Gasperini with a new attacking winger. Inter, Atalanta, and Lazio are also reportedly interested in the 2021 European champion, while the player is reportedly keen on a return to Juventus. Complicating the former Juventus player’s potential arrival in the capital are Liverpool’s demands, which have so far valued the Italian at around €15 million, along with a salary of €7.5 million per season. Roma, on the other hand, are reportedly keen to strengthen their attack through a loan with an option to buy.

top.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning - SEC Football Kickoff Media Day © IMAGN Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning endured another difficult outing in the 16-6 win against Texas A&M. The quarterback struggled offensively in the Lone Star Showdown at Kyle Field on Friday. Coming off an impressive 287-yard, two-touchdown performance against Arkansas, Manning’s pass production was challenged by the Aggies. The Longhorns quarterback completed 18 of 34 passes for 143 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. Manning threw an end-zone interception to Texas A&M defensive back Tawfiq Byard, giving the Aggies a chance at a comeback in the final quarter. Fans reacted to the quarterback’s struggle in the Aggies’ game. “Arch is collapsing. Oh no. Give credit to this A&M defense, but Arch needs to understand they just need to win the game. My goodness,” one fan added. “He has zero football awareness, geez. Anything but an interception and game over,” one fan commented. “Put in Lacey,” one fan noted. “He gonna be the reason Texas don’t win,” one fan remarked. “I actually hope Jerry drafts him,” one fan joked. Manning’s struggles against LSU raised the question of whether the Longhorns quarterback can deliver against elite opponents. top.title: Winning is the only option for Iraola ahead of first Merseyside derby
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola gestures on the touchline during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Fenerbahce and Liverpool at Sukru Saracoglu Stadium. Just two defeats in the last 34 meetings with Everton mean expectations for the short trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium are high. Most of the statistics associated with England’s most-played derby favour the Reds, looking for a fourth successive victory over their neighbours for the first time since August 1991, as the Toffees have won just one of the last 15 home encounters against Liverpool. As a proud Basque, Iraola knows the significance of local rivalries, but Sunday’s game is on an all together higher level. “I played a lot, also a big derby – Athletic [Bilbao]-Real Sociedad. I think they are special because – the same as here – you have a lot of friends that are from the opposing team, sometimes a member of your family even,” he said. “Definitely it’s a game that lasts longer. It’s not a game you play and, OK, you speak a little bit next week. “No, normally this thing lasts long and the winner reminds the other side normally a lot of time. “I experienced it a lot as a player and this is going to be my first one here, but I can feel everyone wants to win it, yes.” Liverpool’s form is encouraging as they have won their last three in all competitions while Everton go into the game off the back of a 4-0 humbling by Brentford, their first defeat in four matches in all competitions. The two teams were separated by five places and five points heading into the weekend but Iraola will not allow his fourth-placed side to be complacent. “I think it is a derby and derbies are always different. It doesn’t matter where you are in the standings, it doesn’t matter the run that you are in,” he added. Four players – Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo, Bradley Barcola and Trey Nyoni – look set for their derby debuts. The 21-year-old Jacquet has slotted into the centre of defence to become Virgil van Dijk’s regular partner and has impressed but his composure will be tested in the derby, although Iraola does not believe the occasion will trouble him. “He has this self-confidence. He is also improving with the language and that always helps with communications with team-mates,” he said of the newly capped France international. “He doesn’t have a lot of games or experience, but he is in high-level games and playing with the national team. “Also, he has help from experienced players around him. That helps when you are young, but he is giving back with performances.”

top.title: Baylor Set to Name Multi-Time Conference Champion as Next Head Coach
top.description: DALLAS, TEXAS - DECEMBER 26: Head coach Jeff Traylor of the UTSA Roadrunners reacts during the second quarter F in the 2025 SERVPRO First Responder Bowl at Gerald J. Ford Stadium on December 26, 2025 in Dallas, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) Getty One of the open Power Four coaching jobs is set to be filled, at least that’s according to ESPN’s Pete Thamel as of Friday night. According to Thamel, Baylor is going to hire UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor as the school’s next leader. Baylor Set to Hire UTSA’s Jeff Traylor as Their Next Head Coach With an official announcement expected to take place in the coming days, Traylor will stay in Texas and jump up the Big 12 after posting a 63-28 record in seven seasons with the Roadrunners. He has UTSA at 10-2 and about to play for a conference title in the American Championship Game. Another win and Traylor, 58, would have his highest victory total since 2022, back when his team finished 11-3 after a loss in the Cure Bowl. But no matter how 2026 ends, Traylor has proven to be a consistent winner at the Group of 5 level. Traylor Turned UTSA Into a Championship Program In seven seasons, he owns a career winning clip of .689, has capped off every season with a bowl appearance, has three-straight bowl wins and two conference championships (both when a member of Conference USA). Before joining UTSA ahead of the 2020 campaign, Traylor served as Arkansas’ assistant head coach and running backs coach in 2018 and 2019. He served in the same position at SMU in 2017 and was a social teams coach at the University of Texas in 2015 and 2016. Traylor started his coaching career working up the Texas high school ranks in the late 1990s, eventually landing a head role at Gilmer High School from 2000-2014. And while Traylor may not be a flashy name nationally, he will now be able to test his system and recruiting chops with resources at his disposal. Aranda was 40-40 overall and 26-32 in conference play in six seasons. Never able to duplicate his second year, when he led the Bears to a 12-2 record, a Big 12 title and a victory in the Sugar Bowl, Aranda was 4-3 in 2026 at the time of his dismissal, a disappointing start to a season that followed going 5-7 in 2025. Aranda only reached a bowl game in three seasons, losing his most recent opportunities in 2022 and 2024. top.title: 2027: SDP candidate promises N200 petrol, free healthcare
top.description: The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Dr Adewole Adebayo, has promised to reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy and provide free healthcare if elected president in 2027. He also pledged free and compulsory education, increased food production, job creation and improved welfare for persons living with disabilities. Adebayo made the promises at an SDP town hall meeting with party leaders, candidates and supporters in Nasarawa State. He urged Nigerians to use the 2027 general election to determine the country’s leadership through the ballot, stressing the importance of electoral participation. Adebayo said the SDP had developed policy proposals to address poverty, unemployment, high living costs and other economic challenges facing the country. On fuel pricing, he said an SDP-led government would reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy through improved efficiency and measures to address corruption in the petroleum sector. “We will give you petrol for N200 per litre without subsidy. We will sell it for N200, and NNPC will still make a profit because we will stop funding corruption,” he said. On agriculture, Adebayo said Nasarawa and neighbouring states had the potential to contribute significantly to national food production. “Nasarawa alone can feed Nigeria. Nasarawa, Plateau, Kogi, Kaduna and the Federal Capital Territory have the capacity to feed the whole of Africa,” he said. He also promised free and compulsory education, including measures to expand access to schooling for out-of-school children. According to him, an SDP administration would integrate children in the Almajiri system into formal education while ensuring they continued to receive religious instruction. On healthcare, Adebayo proposed establishing a Federal Medical Centre in every federal constituency and introducing compulsory medical check-ups four times annually. He also promised free medical consultations and medication, although he did not provide details of the proposed funding arrangements. On employment, the SDP candidate pledged to create more job opportunities, including for individuals living with disabilities. He also promised to develop Nasarawa’s mineral resources, including gold, coal, lithium and copper, to promote economic growth and improve the welfare of host communities. top.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic Breaks Silence After Tense Altercation With Spurs Fan
top.description: The Lakers provide a new Luka Doncic injury update ahead of Sunday's Suns game. Coach JJ Redick addresses the star's condition and potential availability. Getty A tense altercation between Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic and a San Antonio Spurs fan stole the spotlight Friday night, overshadowing a thriller between the West’s top two seeds that ended in a narrow San Antonio win. As Doncic walked toward the tunnel following the 99-96 loss, a woman appeared to say something to him, prompting the Lakers star to toss a wristband her way. He continued walking before abruptly turning back to confront her and demand the wristband back. A man seated next to her then shoved Doncic in the shoulder, drawing several Lakers players into the fray. Jarred Vanderbilt quickly stepped in to shield Doncic as teammates and security intervened to separate the group. Doncic seemingly mistook the woman for a fan, though she clearly wasn’t one. View this post on Instagram Luka Doncic Explains Tense Moment After the game, Doncic explained that he tossed the sweatband to the woman assuming she wanted a souvenir, noting he routinely hands them to courtside fans after games. “I just threw my wristband, like I do almost every game,” Doncic said, via The Athletic. “And then I heard she didn’t want it so I went back to grab it. And then he pushed me. And then I gave it to somebody else,” added Doncic. View this post on Instagram The postgame incident capped one of Doncic’s worst shooting nights of the season, as the NBA MVP frontrunner went 1-of-13 from three and needed 31 shots to score as many points. After catching fire in the first half, he struggled to penetrate San Antonio’s defense after the break. As a result, Los Angeles was outscored 61-42 over the final 24 minutes, squandering a commanding 54-38 halftime lead. nigeria.title: Pete Edochie: Linc breaks down in tears as unusual calm rules Enugu residence
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku & By Dennis Agbo Linc Edochie, the third son of the late Pete Edochie, could not hold back his tears when he saw his father’s corpse in the mortuary. The movie legend died in the early hours of Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. He had taken ill and was rushed to a hospital in Enugu, where he passed away. Painting a gloomy picture of the atmosphere at the late actor’s riverside residence in Trans-Ekulu, Enugu-based actor and filmmaker, Steve Eboh, said Linc broke down the moment he sighted his father’s body. “When Linc stormed the mortuary and sighted his father’s corpse, he cried profusely and leaned on his brother’s shoulder. We consoled him and prayed for the family,” Eboh said. Eboh added that grief was written all over the faces of people whose lives Pete Edochie had touched during his acting career. “We thank God for a life well spent. He was a legend who touched so many lives. He was not just an actor, he was a global icon. Everybody knew him.” Our correspondent, who visited the late actor’s Trans-Ekulu residence, described a gloomy picture of desertion and sorrow. “Apart from a domestic aide seen at the premises, there was little indication of the tragic development that had thrown the family and the Nigerian entertainment industry into mourning,” he noted. A source familiar with the circumstances surrounding his death told our correspondent that the actor took ill on Tuesday night and was subsequently rushed to a hospital in Enugu, where he died at about 12:30am on Wednesday. According to the source, Edochie’s family had remained at the hospital since his death, apparently attending to necessary arrangements and coming to terms with the loss. The family’s absence from the residence accounted for the quiet atmosphere observed during the reporter’s visit. nigeria.title: Why I turned down Burna Boy’s 85/15 demand – Aristokrat boss, Peedi Picasso
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku Peedi Picasso, CEO of Aristokrat Records, has opened up on why he refused to renew Burna Boy’s record deal, saying the singer demanded an 85-15 per cent revenue split in his favour. Picasso, whose real name is Piriye Isokrari said their previous deal gave Burna Boy 60 per cent, while the label took 40 per cent. He also revealed that the singer’s mother insisted he should only sign two-year contracts, a condition that influenced the label’s decision. According to Picasso, the proposed increase did not make financial sense at the time because the label was not making significant money from record sales. Picasso said live performances and endorsement deals were the major sources of revenue. He argued that accepting an 80-20 or 85-15 split would have left the label with a smaller share of the income despite the money it was investing in the singer. Picasso said the arrangement was difficult to justify for another two-year contract, particularly because the label was not entering a long-term deal. nigeria.title: A Weekend For Proof
nigeria.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and other opposition leaders are expected at the November 30 summit. Their attendance and any signed commitments remain forthcoming. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations.

nigeria.title: Trump proposes new tariffs on China, EU, 12 others
nigeria.description: By Vera Anyagafu US President Donald Trump has proposed a new round of tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China and the European Union. The proposals were announced on Wednesday, November 25, by the Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) after an eight-month investigation into what Washington calls ‘structural excess capacity’. The US says the targeted countries are promoting production through subsidies and other industrial policies, allowing them to flood world markets with cheap goods and undercut American manufacturers. The 14 economies targeted are China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. Mexico and Norway were also investigated but have been spared for now. China faces a proposed rate of 20 per cent on most products, which would be added to tariffs imposed during Trump’s first term, but would not stack on top of more recent forced-labour tariffs. According to a senior US official, the rate could double to 40 per cent if talks between Washington and Beijing fall apart. Products from the EU will be taxed at 15 per cent in compliance with the US deal with the bloc, though USTR said that could also rise to as much as 20 per cent. The new tariffs are being proposed under Section 301 of the 1974 US Trade Act, which allows Washington to penalise countries it determines are treating US businesses unfairly. The proposals are still subject to a public comment process, with comments closing on January 5, 2027, and a public hearing starting January 25, 2027, before any final action. However, Beijing has rejected the accusations, with Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun saying the so-called overcapacity is a false issue, and China opposes using it as an excuse for political manipulation. According to him, the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. INEC had earlier published the list of polling units selected for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, FCT. The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS. The exercise is expected to stimulate the Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The INEC chairman called on the Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioners and the Commissioners of Police in the states to take part fully. “I urge all Resident Electoral Commissioners and Commissioners of Police to treat November 28 as a full-scale operational rehearsal: test your communication lines, evaluate rapid-response times around mock polling centres, and identify any logistical or security blind spots while there is still ample time to resolve them,” he said. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps. Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. business.title: Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. business.title: New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Maresca praises Arsenal but hopes Man City can match champions
sports.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca gestures during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester City and Napoli at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Maresca praises Arsenal but hopes Man City can match champions») Mike Egerton/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca accepts Manchester City are some way behind Arsenal in their development - but is determined to match the champions this weekend. City, who travel to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday, have fallen six points behind the Gunners at the top of the Premier League after failing to win their last four matches. It is an abrupt downturn in form after City opened their campaign with seven successive victories, but Maresca believes their relative lack of experience together helps explain their recent difficulties. The City manager, who succeeded Pep Guardiola in the summer, said: “They won the Premier League, played the Champions League final, so that shows how good they are in this moment. “We’re going to try our best to win the game but no doubt in this moment, because they won the Premier League, they are the best. “For two-and-a-half months we were top of the league. Now we are not there and everyone is comparing. That is correct but, for me, it is seven years together against four months together. You cannot compare. “We already showed [our strength] this season in winning important games away – at Old Trafford and Anfield, two important away games. “Sunday is another important one, we showed already and we can win again.” Maresca says he has been happy enough with his side’s general play, but their failure to convert chances and occasional defensive lapses are proving costly. He said: “The problem for us has been [the difference] between what we create and what we concede. “We need to try to be solid, don’t concede, and with the quality that we have, and the amount of chances that we create every game, for sure we need to be more clinical and score more goals. “We need to win duels, second balls and show personality, but this is a nice game for us to see where we are in term of personality and to try to understand the situation more.” City can ill afford to lose if they are to keep pace with the Gunners but Maresca is more concerned about the bigger picture than the immediate ramifications for the title race. He said: “Because we won seven or eight games in a row at the beginning the transition looks more easy, but it is a transition. “Where we can be on Sunday night if we win or draw is important, 100%, but for us it’s a long season and we will see where are in February or March and from there you can set the goals. “Now it’s useless to speak about a target or where we can be at the end of the season.”

sports.description: In defence of Red Bull and its footballing exploits As the Bundesliga’s most controversial member, Die Roten Bullen continue to operate effectively in a hostile environment. Measuring success strictly through silverware is a difficult task, but combing through historic transfer business – in some cases via picturesque Salzburg – tells a rather specific tale. Defined by exits more so than arrivals, the club appears to provide a platform for talent while consistently living up to the brand’s familiar slogan. Dayot Upamecano, arguably the most adept central defender at this moment in time, departed for Bavaria after four seasons in Leipzig. Joshua Kimmich plied his trade there, firstly in 3. Liga and 2. Bundesliga before eventually coming of age in Bayern colours. One other Munich-based player, the plucky and tenacious Konrad Laimer, spent six campaigns in that divisive shirt prior to his free transfer. sports.title: Xabi Alonso admits Chelsea are low on confidence after third straight defeat at Nottingham Forest
sports.description: Xabi Alonso admits Chelsea are low on confidence after third straight defeat at Nottingham Forest Xabi Alonso has admitted that Chelsea are low on confidence after losing 3-2 at Nottingham Forest. Chelsea lost a third consecutive game at the City Ground on Friday night as the club's poor run of form continued. Igor Jesus volleyed Forest ahead inside five minutes, before Morgan Gibbs-White doubled the lead from the penalty spot early in the second half, after Wesley Fofana brought down former Chelsea forward Liam Delap in the area. Emmanuel Emegha pulled one back for the Blues, but a second from Gibbs-White restored Forest's advantage. Emegha was on target again, heading home from Cole Palmer's cross, but Chelsea were unable to find an equaliser. Defeat increases the pressure on Alonso, whose side have now conceded 23 goals in just 12 league games. Only Crystal Palace have conceded more in the Premier League , ahead of the weekend's fixtures. Chelsea are eighth in the Premier League table, five points adrift of the Champions League places, having played a game more than fourth-placed Liverpool. Alonso urges Chelsea to find solutions after Forest defeat extends losing streak to three games Reflecting on the result, Alonso said his side are suffering from a crisis of confidence. "Many things didn’t go the way we wanted," the Spaniard said in his post-match interview. "I think we are low in confidence; you see that the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting [a goal back for] the 2-1, we then conceded the 3-1 just when we had a little bit of boost from the goal. "We can do better for sure. At this level, you need to hold results and you don’t have to concede that much. That is why we are losing the last games. "So, everything is not going our way. We are responsible for that, and we are responsible for trying to find solutions."

sports.title: Gaza’s chess players survive a genocide and rebuild a community
sports.description: Gaza City – Raghad Rabie, 18, never expected to beat her chess coach, Raghad Adas, at chess. During the friendly match, Rabie deliberately left some of her pieces exposed to distract her opponent as she planned a move that would deliver a checkmate in two turns. Her strategy worked, giving her confidence in her abilities as a chess player. But the match also reflected something bigger: The return of chess to Gaza after the Israeli genocide devastated sporting activities across the enclave. Rabie began learning chess in August 2025, when she was displaced in southern Gaza. Looking for something new to learn and a way to occupy her time, she taught herself the basic rules online before joining a training course run by Adas. “I had admired chess players for a long time and wanted to learn the game. I started on my own, then the course helped me improve,” she says. She has since participated in two tournaments and dreams of becoming a chess grandmaster, the goal of every serious chess player, and representing Palestine internationally. But pursuing that ambition in Gaza, still under an Israeli siege and subject to daily air attacks despite an October 2025 “ceasefire”, is difficult. There is no permanent training venue for chess players, so weekly gatherings take place in different locations, including the Lord Cafe in the al-Rimal neighbourhood of Gaza City. Raghad Rabie, 18, one of the chess players at Stalemate [Lina Abu Zayed/Al Jazeera] To become an International Chess Federation (FIDE)-rated grandmaster, as Rabie hopes, requires thousands of hours of dedicated practice and study. But a shortage of chessboards, clocks and chess books – and soaring prices for any available chess equipment – has made this mission difficult. Before the war, Adas was captain of the girls’ Spark team, playing in Palestinian Chess Federation tournaments. She was also among 10 players selected to take part in matches against other Palestinians from the occupied West Bank with the goal of forming a national team, which it was hoped would compete internationally. Travel arrangements and permit procedures had been completed, but then Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza broke out in October 2023, killing at least 74,000 Palestinians and laying waste to the Palestinian enclave. “I was excited about taking part in an international tournament, but the war made everything much more difficult,” Adas told Al Jazeera. Adas said the team’s headquarters was destroyed, its players were scattered across Gaza, and she lost contact with several former teammates amid the forced Israeli displacements. About a year after the war began, Adas started teaching chess in shelters, initially volunteering before working with organisations and eventually continuing her mission independently. sports.title: Lakers are ‘real’ deal — even Victor Wembanyama thinks so
sports.description: Like the rest of us, Victor Wembanyama was skeptical of the Lakers. The darlings of the NBA entered Friday’s game against the Spurs with the top record in the NBA at 15-3. But they hadn’t played the league’s most elite teams. They hadn’t really proven themselves. So, Friday was a temperature check. It was a harsh dressing room mirror that would expose their flaws in front of a national television audience. How did they do? “As a team I wasn’t sure what they were built of, at least from the start of the season,” Wembanyama acknowledged. “But it’s real.” The Lakers lost, 99-96 . But the final score was far less important than what transpired. The Lakers led by as much as 20 points. They bottled up Wembanyama in the first half, holding him to just eight points on nine shot attempts and five rebounds. Over that period, Luka Dončić had as many rebounds as Wembanyama (five) while scoring more than twice as many points (19). It was incredible. The Spurs reached the Finals last year. Wembanyama is unequivocally considered the next face of the league once the 41-year-old LeBron James retires. This was about as big of a test as the Lakers could get. And at the beginning of the game, they were jaw-droppingly good. Then things fell apart. The Lakers were outscored in the third quarter, 30-14. Over that period, they were outshot from the field, 48.1% to 25%, and from beyond the 3-point line, 37.5% to 15.4%. They unraveled, culminating in Keldon Johnson making a 3-pointer with 1.8 seconds left to knot the score at 68-68 heading into the fourth quarter. The next 12 minutes were a dogfight. Both teams wanted this. Victor Wembanyama (left) and Luka Dončić look on during the Lakers’ 99-96 NBA Cup loss to the Spurs on Nov. 27, 2026, in San Antonio. NBAE via Getty Images Wembanyama and Dončić, who are in a two-horse race for the MVP Award , knew the stakes. Everyone on the court was acutely aware of the chatter this game would generate. They knew this contest meant so much more than another regular-season game in November. Ultimately, the Spurs clawed a few inches ahead as the final buzzer sounded. After Wembanyama’s sluggish start, he finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, four steals and two blocked shots. But he had as many field-goal attempts (25) as points. Dončić had a game-high 31 points, six rebounds, eight assists and three steals. But he went 1-for-13 from beyond the arc. Luka Dončić looks to make a move on De’Aaron Fox during the Lakers’ NBA Cup road loss to the Spurs. AP Photo/Darren Abate Both of them shined. Both of them struggled. The Spurs likely prevailed because they’ve experienced moments like this before. They were three wins away from a championship last year. If they hadn’t blown double-digit leads in all five of their games against the Knicks in the Finals, they would’ve been the reigning champions. According to a report from The Athletic (h/t SPORT ), Arsenal view the 22-year-old Spaniard as a possible long-term successor to Ben White, and it is a development that could complicate Barcelona’s long-standing interest in a player they have followed since his breakthrough at Real Valladolid. Arsenal identify Fresneda as a future option at right back As reported by the outlet, Arsenal are assessing their right-back options as part of their longer-term squad planning.
